  1356	// runTrailUpdateWithClientAtPath applies a trail update once the repo route and
  1357	// API client are resolved.
  1358	func runTrailUpdateWithClientAtPath(ctx context.Context, w, errW io.Writer, client *api.Client, basePath string, inputs trailUpdateInputs) error {
  1359		// Determine branch.
  1360		branch := inputs.Branch
  1361		if branch == "" {
  1362			current, err := GetCurrentBranch(ctx)
  1363			if err != nil {
  1364				return fmt.Errorf("failed to determine current branch: %w", err)
  1365			}
  1366			branch = current
  1367		}
  1368	
  1369		// Find the trail by branch.
  1370		found, err := findTrailByBranchAtPath(ctx, client, basePath, branch)
  1371		if err != nil {
  1372			return err
  1373		}
  1374		if found == nil {
  1375			return fmt.Errorf("no trail found for branch %q", branch)
  1376		}
  1377	
  1378		// Interactive mode when no update flags are provided.
  1379		statusStr := inputs.Status
  1380		title := inputs.Title
  1381		body := inputs.Body
  1382		var bodyETag string
  1383		noFlags := !inputs.StatusChanged && !inputs.TitleChanged && !inputs.BodyChanged &&
  1384			inputs.AssigneeAdd == nil && inputs.AssigneeRemove == nil &&
  1385			inputs.ReviewerAdd == nil && inputs.ReviewerRemove == nil &&
  1386			!inputs.TypeChanged && !inputs.PriorityChanged
  1387		if noFlags {
  1388			metadata := found.ToMetadata()
  1389			// Build status options with current value as default.
  1390			var statusOptions []huh.Option[string]
  1391			for _, s := range trail.ValidStatuses() {
  1392				if (s == trail.StatusMerged || s == trail.StatusClosed) && s != metadata.Status {
  1393					continue
  1394				}
  1395				label := string(s)
  1396				if s == metadata.Status {
  1397					label += " (current)"
  1398				}
  1399				statusOptions = append(statusOptions, huh.NewOption(label, string(s)))
  1400			}
  1401			statusStr = string(metadata.Status)
  1402			title = metadata.Title
  1403			// The list resource omits the description; fetch the detail body so
  1404			// the form prefills with the current text and change detection below
  1405			// compares against the real server value. Warn on a fetch failure so
  1406			// a blank baseline doesn't silently overwrite an unseen description.
  1407			seedBody, seedETag, bodyErr := resolveTrailUpdateBodyAtPath(ctx, client, basePath, found)
  1408			if bodyErr != nil {
  1409				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: could not load current trail body: %v\n", bodyErr)
  1410			}
  1411			body = seedBody
  1412			bodyETag = seedETag
  1413			origStatus, origTitle, origBody := statusStr, title, body
  1414	
  1415			form := NewAccessibleForm(
  1416				huh.NewGroup(
  1417					huh.NewSelect[string]().
  1418						Title("Status").
  1419						Options(statusOptions...).
  1420						Value(&statusStr),
  1421					huh.NewInput().
  1422						Title("Title").
  1423						Value(&title),
  1424					huh.NewText().
  1425						Title("Body").
  1426						Value(&body),
  1427				),
  1428			)
  1429			if formErr := form.Run(); formErr != nil {
  1430				return handleFormCancellation(w, "Trail update", formErr)
  1431			}
  1432			// Only mark a field changed when the user actually edited it, so an
  1433			// untouched body/title/status isn't needlessly PATCHed (a no-op body
  1434			// PATCH would otherwise rewrite the description on every update).
  1435			inputs.StatusChanged = statusStr != origStatus
  1436			inputs.TitleChanged = title != origTitle
  1437			inputs.BodyChanged = body != origBody
  1438		}
  1439	
  1440		statusStr = strings.TrimSpace(statusStr)
  1441		title = strings.TrimSpace(title)
  1442		if err := validateTrailUpdateFields(trailUpdateInputs{
  1443			Status:          statusStr,
  1444			StatusChanged:   inputs.StatusChanged,
  1445			Title:           title,
  1446			TitleChanged:    inputs.TitleChanged,
  1447			Type:            inputs.Type,
  1448			TypeChanged:     inputs.TypeChanged,
  1449			Priority:        inputs.Priority,
  1450			PriorityChanged: inputs.PriorityChanged,
  1451		}); err != nil {
  1452			return err
  1453		}
  1454	
  1455		// Build the metadata request with only changed fields. The description is
  1456		// not part of it — it is written separately, from the `body` local below.
  1457		updateReq := buildTrailUpdateRequest(found, trailUpdateInputs{
  1458			Status:          statusStr,
  1459			StatusChanged:   inputs.StatusChanged,
  1460			Title:           title,
  1461			TitleChanged:    inputs.TitleChanged,
  1462			AssigneeAdd:     inputs.AssigneeAdd,
  1463			AssigneeRemove:  inputs.AssigneeRemove,
  1464			ReviewerAdd:     inputs.ReviewerAdd,
  1465			ReviewerRemove:  inputs.ReviewerRemove,
  1466			Type:            inputs.Type,
  1467			TypeChanged:     inputs.TypeChanged,
  1468			Priority:        inputs.Priority,
  1469			PriorityChanged: inputs.PriorityChanged,
  1470		})
  1471	
  1472		// The single-trail endpoint is keyed by trail number, not id; the server
  1473		// rejects an id here with "Invalid trail number format".
  1474		if found.Number <= 0 {
  1475			return fmt.Errorf("trail for branch %q has no number yet; cannot update", branch)
  1476		}
  1477		path := trailNumberPathForBase(basePath, found.Number)
  1478	
  1479		// Metadata and description live on different routes, so an update touching
  1480		// both sends two requests. They are not atomic: if the metadata PATCH lands
  1481		// and the body PUT then fails, the metadata change persists. Report that
  1482		// partial state explicitly so the caller knows the metadata already applied
  1483		// and only the body needs a retry, rather than assuming nothing changed.
  1484		hasMeta := trailUpdateRequestHasFields(updateReq)
  1485		if !hasMeta && !inputs.BodyChanged {
  1486			// Nothing changed — most often the interactive form opened and closed
  1487			// untouched. Say so instead of printing the success line: no request went
  1488			// out, and agents read that line as confirmation the write landed.
  1489			fmt.Fprintf(w, "No changes to apply to the trail for branch %s\n", branch)
  1490			return nil
  1491		}
  1492		if hasMeta {
  1493			if err := sendTrailPatch(ctx, client, path, updateReq); err != nil {
  1494				return err
  1495			}
  1496		}
  1497		if !noFlags && inputs.BodyChanged && bodyETag == "" && !inputs.Overwrite {
  1498			// Non-interactive --body path only (noFlags is the interactive
  1499			// branch, which already read the body and its etag above to seed the
  1500			// editor — gating on that branch rather than on bodyETag=="" matters:
  1501			// an interactive session can legitimately end with no etag too (e.g.
  1502			// the seed read failed and the user was already warned), and redoing
  1503			// the read here would silently pair an etag for content the user
  1504			// never saw with their edit). A --body caller supplied the
  1505			// replacement text directly and skipped that read, so do it here,
  1506			// best-effort, purely for the etag. A failure just leaves bodyETag
  1507			// empty and falls through to sendTrailBody's graceful Overwrite
  1508			// fallback rather than failing the whole command — but say so, since
  1509			// this is the unattended path most likely to run without anyone
  1510			// watching for a silently downgraded conflict check.
  1511			if _, etag, ferr := fetchTrailDescriptionAtPath(ctx, client, basePath, found.Number); ferr != nil {
  1512				fmt.Fprintf(errW, "Warning: could not verify trail body is unchanged (%v); writing without conflict detection\n", ferr)
  1513			} else {
  1514				bodyETag = etag
  1515			}
  1516		}
  1517		if inputs.BodyChanged {
  1518			if err := sendTrailBody(ctx, client, trailBodyPathForBase(basePath, found.Number), body, bodyETag, inputs.Overwrite); err != nil {
  1519				if hasMeta {
  1520					return fmt.Errorf("trail metadata was updated, but the body update failed (the metadata change already applied; retry only the --body change): %w", err)
  1521				}
  1522				return err
  1523			}
  1524		}
  1525	
  1660	func sendTrailPatch(ctx context.Context, client *api.Client, path string, req api.TrailUpdateRequest) error {
  1661		resp, err := client.Patch(ctx, path, req)
  1662		if err != nil {
  1663			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update trail: %w", err)
  1664		}
  1665		defer resp.Body.Close()
  1666		if err := checkTrailResponse(resp); err != nil {
  1667			return err
  1668		}
  1669		var updateResp api.TrailUpdateResponse
  1670		if err := api.DecodeJSON(resp, &updateResp); err != nil {
  1671			return fmt.Errorf("failed to decode update response: %w", err)
  1672		}
  1673		return nil
  1674	}
  1675	
  1676	// sendTrailBody writes a trail's description through the body route, the only
  1677	// one that serves body writes (api.TrailUpdateRequest documents why the metadata
  1678	// PATCH does not). path must already be that route — see trailBodyPath.
  1679	//
  1680	// Three dispatch modes, in order:
  1681	//
  1682	//   - overwrite: sends Overwrite: true and no If-Match. This is the explicit
  1683	//     --overwrite flag — the caller wants the replacement to win regardless of
  1684	//     what's there.
  1685	//   - ifMatch non-empty (and !overwrite): sends If-Match instead of Overwrite,
  1686	//     so the write is rejected with 412 if the description changed since
  1687	//     ifMatch was read (resolveTrailUpdateBody / the non-interactive etag
  1688	//     fetch in runTrailUpdateWithClient).
  1689	//   - neither: falls back to Overwrite: true. This is deliberate graceful
  1690	//     degradation, not a shortcut to remove — it's what runs against a server
  1691	//     that predates the etag field, a trail with no body document yet, or
  1692	//     after a failed best-effort etag read. Refusing to write in that case
  1693	//     would make `trail update --body` unusable against anything older or
  1694	//     partial than the newest server.
  1695	func sendTrailBody(ctx context.Context, client *api.Client, path, body, ifMatch string, overwrite bool) error {
  1696		req := api.TrailBodyRequest{Markdown: body}
  1697		var headers http.Header
  1698		if ifMatch != "" && !overwrite {
  1699			headers = http.Header{"If-Match": []string{ifMatch}}
  1700		} else {
  1701			req.Overwrite = true
  1702		}
  1703	
  1704		data, err := json.Marshal(req)
  1705		if err != nil {
  1706			return fmt.Errorf("marshal trail body request: %w", err)
  1707		}
  1708		resp, err := client.Request(ctx, http.MethodPut, path, headers, bytes.NewReader(data))
  1709		if err != nil {
  1710			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update trail body: %w", err)
  1711		}
  1712		defer resp.Body.Close()
  1713		if err := checkTrailResponse(resp); err != nil {
  1714			switch {
  1715			case api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusPreconditionFailed):
  1716				return fmt.Errorf("%w — trail body changed since it was read; run 'entire trail show' to see the current text and merge it in, then re-run — or pass --overwrite to discard it", err)
  1717			case api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusConflict):
  1718				return fmt.Errorf("%w — trail body is not empty; pass --overwrite to replace it", err)
  1719			default:
  1720				return err
  1721			}
  1722		}
  1723		// Nothing reads the document back; decoding it only confirms the success
  1724		// really was this route's JSON response, and drains the body — the same
  1725		// check sendTrailPatch makes on the metadata route.

GitHub has no open issue or PR matching this exact failure mode; PR #2079 remains the source of the fallback, and draft PR #1493 remains broader and unmerged. Entire Review:

Reviewing `fix-trail-context-overwrite` vs live `upstream/main`: 0 branch commits, 3 intended Trail files changed, plus 2 unrelated configuration files excluded from the fix.

Initial findings: no blocker in the intended patch. The old code converts a failed verification read into overwrite authority and can PATCH metadata before learning that body verification failed. The patch restores the stated invariant by returning before the form or any mutation, and by reserving `overwrite: true` for explicit `--overwrite`.

Compatibility is supported, not guessed: merged PR #2055 records deployed behavior before ETags existed. A no-overwrite body PUT succeeds for an empty document and returns `409 document_not_empty` for a nonempty document. PR #2079 then added ETags without removing that guarded mode. That supports both old-server and current-server use when a successful detail response has no ETag. I recommend keeping the patch as implemented and proceeding to verification and final reviews. No production edit is indicated at this point.

No production correctness defect found in the fail-closed change. The focused tests exercise the real command and HTTP request-building paths.

## Test-contract audit

The tests call production functions directly, use the real API client, and mock only the external HTTP boundary:

- `runTrailUpdateWithClientAtPath` performs the verification before either mutation at [trail_cmd.go:1490](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-trail-context-overwrite/cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd.go:1490).

- Non-interactive detail GET failure: title plus body input, detail returns 500, actual PATCH count `0`, PUT count `0`, and error contains `could not verify trail body is unchanged` ([test:2723](/Users/muskanpaliwal/Work/open-source/entire/cli/fix-trail-context-overwrite/cmd/entire/cli/trail_cmd_test.go:2723)).

     1	# Contributing to the Entire CLI
     2	
     3	Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.
     4	
     5	Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.
     6	
     7	> **New to Entire?** See the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Before You Code: Discuss First
    12	
    13	The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.
    14	
    15	### Contribution Workflow
    16	
    17	1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
    18	2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
    19	3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
    20	4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
    21	5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
    22	6. **Maintainer review and merge**
    23	
    24	---
    25	
    26	## First-Time Contributors
    27	
    28	**New to open source or to Entire?** Start with the [First-Time Contributors Guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It walks through the full path: finding an issue, forking, setting up your dev environment, opening a PR, and what to expect afterwards.
    29	
    30	The rest of this document is the reference for ongoing contributors.
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## Submitting Issues
    35	
    36	All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.
    37	
    38	For security-related issues, see the Security section below.
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## Security
    43	
    44	If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.
    45	
    46	---
    47	
    48	## Contributions & Communication
    49	
    50	Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:
    51	
    52	- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
    53	- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support
    54	
    55	Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.
    56	
    57	
    58	## How to Contribute
    59	
    60	
    61	There are many ways to contribute:
    62	
    63	- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
    64	- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
    65	- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
    66	- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
    67	- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge
    68	
    69	
    70	## Reporting Bugs
    71	
    72	Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:
    73	
    74	### Required Information
    75	
    76	1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
    77	2. **Operating system**
    78	3. **Go version** - run `go version`
    79	
    80	### What to Include
    81	
    82	Please answer these questions in your bug report:
    83	
    84	1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
    85	2. **What did you expect to happen?**
    86	3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
    87	4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
    88	5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues
    89	
    90	---
    91	
    92	## Local Setup
    93	
    94	### Prerequisites
    95	
    96	- **Go 1.27.1+** - Check with `go version`. `go.mod` pins the minimum, so an older toolchain fails unless it can download the pinned one (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local` cannot).
    97	- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
    98	
    99	### Clone and Install
   100	
   101	```bash
   102	# Clone the repository
   103	git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
   104	cd cli
   105	
   106	# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
   107	mise trust
   108	
   109	# Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
   110	mise install
   111	
   112	# Download Go modules
   113	go mod download
   114	
   115	# Build the CLI
   116	mise run build
   117	
   118	# Verify setup by running tests
   119	mise run test
   120	```
   121	
   122	> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for detailed architecture and development reference.
   123	
   124	---
   125	
   126	## Making Changes
   127	
   128	1. **Create a branch** for your changes:
   129	   ```bash
   130	   git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
   131	   ```
   132	
   133	2. **Make your changes** - follow the [Code Style](#code-style) guidelines
   134	
   135	3. **Test your changes** - see [Testing](#testing)
   136	
   137	4. **Commit** with clear, descriptive messages:
   138	   ```bash
   139	   git commit -m "Add feature: description of what you added"
   140	   ```
   141	
   142	---
   143	
   144	## Code Style
   145	
   146	Follow standard Go idioms and conventions. For detailed guidance, see the **Go Code Style** section in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).
   147	
   148	### Key Points
   149	
   150	- **Error handling**: Handle all errors explicitly - don't leave them unchecked
   151	- **Formatting**: Code must pass `gofmt` (run `mise run fmt`)
   152	- **Linting**: Code must pass `golangci-lint` (run `mise run lint`)
   153	- **Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names following Go conventions
   154	
   155	---
   156	
   157	## Testing
   158	
   159	> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for complete testing documentation.
   160	
   161	```bash
   162	# Unit tests - always run before committing
   163	mise run test
   164	
   165	# Integration tests
   166	mise run test:integration
   167	
   168	# Full CI suite
   169	mise run test:ci
   170	```
   171	
   172	Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
   173	
   174	---
   175	
   176	## Creating an Agent
   177	
   178	
   179	Entire supports two ways to create agents:

     1	# Contributing to the Entire CLI
     2	
     3	Thank you for your interest in contributing to Entire! We welcome contributions from everyone.
     4	
     5	Please read our [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before participating.
     6	
     7	> **New to Entire?** See the [README](README.md) for setup and usage documentation.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Before You Code: Discuss First
    12	
    13	The fastest way to get a contribution merged is to align with maintainers before writing code. Please **open an issue first** using our [issue templates](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/new/choose) and wait for maintainer feedback before starting implementation.
    14	
    15	### Contribution Workflow
    16	
    17	1. **Open an issue** describing the problem or feature
    18	2. **Wait for maintainer feedback** -- we may have relevant context or plans
    19	3. **Get approval** before starting implementation
    20	4. **Submit your PR** referencing the approved issue
    21	5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
    22	6. **Maintainer review and merge**
    23	
    24	---
    25	
    26	## First-Time Contributors
    27	
    28	**New to open source or to Entire?** Start with the [First-Time Contributors Guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It walks through the full path: finding an issue, forking, setting up your dev environment, opening a PR, and what to expect afterwards.
    29	
    30	The rest of this document is the reference for ongoing contributors.
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## Submitting Issues
    35	
    36	All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.
    37	
    38	For security-related issues, see the Security section below.
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## Security
    43	
    44	If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.
    45	
    46	---
    47	
    48	## Contributions & Communication
    49	
    50	Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:
    51	
    52	- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
    53	- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support
    54	
    55	Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.
    56	
    57	
    58	## How to Contribute
    59	
    60	
    61	There are many ways to contribute:
    62	
    63	- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
    64	- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
    65	- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
    66	- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
    67	- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge
    68	
    69	
    70	## Reporting Bugs
    71	
    72	Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:
    73	
    74	### Required Information
    75	
    76	1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
    77	2. **Operating system**
    78	3. **Go version** - run `go version`
    79	
    80	### What to Include
    81	
    82	Please answer these questions in your bug report:
    83	
    84	1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
    85	2. **What did you expect to happen?**
    86	3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
    87	4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
    88	5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues
    89	
    90	---
    91	
    92	## Local Setup
    93	
    94	### Prerequisites
    95	
    96	- **Go 1.27.1+** - Check with `go version`. `go.mod` pins the minimum, so an older toolchain fails unless it can download the pinned one (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local` cannot).
    97	- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
    98	
    99	### Clone and Install
   100	
   101	```bash
   102	# Clone the repository
   103	git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
   104	cd cli
   105	
   106	# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)
   107	mise trust
   108	
   109	# Install dependencies (mise will install the correct Go version)
   110	mise install
   111	
   112	# Download Go modules
   113	go mod download
   114	
   115	# Build the CLI
   116	mise run build
   117	
   118	# Verify setup by running tests
   119	mise run test
   120	```
   121	
   122	> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for detailed architecture and development reference.
   123	
   124	---
   125	
   126	## Making Changes
   127	
   128	1. **Create a branch** for your changes:
   129	   ```bash
   130	   git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name
   131	   ```
   132	
   133	2. **Make your changes** - follow the [Code Style](#code-style) guidelines
   134	
   135	3. **Test your changes** - see [Testing](#testing)
   136	
   137	4. **Commit** with clear, descriptive messages:
   138	   ```bash
   139	   git commit -m "Add feature: description of what you added"
   140	   ```
   141	
   142	---
   143	
   144	## Code Style
   145	
   146	Follow standard Go idioms and conventions. For detailed guidance, see the **Go Code Style** section in [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).
   147	
   148	### Key Points
   149	
   150	- **Error handling**: Handle all errors explicitly - don't leave them unchecked
   151	- **Formatting**: Code must pass `gofmt` (run `mise run fmt`)
   152	- **Linting**: Code must pass `golangci-lint` (run `mise run lint`)
   153	- **Naming**: Use meaningful, descriptive names following Go conventions
   154	
   155	---
   156	
   157	## Testing
   158	
   159	> See [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) for complete testing documentation.
   160	
   161	```bash
   162	# Unit tests - always run before committing
   163	mise run test
   164	
   165	# Integration tests
   166	mise run test:integration
   167	
   168	# Full CI suite
   169	mise run test:ci
   170	```
   171	
   172	Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.
   173	
   174	---

    21	5. **Address all feedback** including automated Copilot comments
    22	6. **Maintainer review and merge**
    23	
    24	---
    25	
    26	## First-Time Contributors
    27	
    28	**New to open source or to Entire?** Start with the [First-Time Contributors Guide](docs/first-time-contributors.md). It walks through the full path: finding an issue, forking, setting up your dev environment, opening a PR, and what to expect afterwards.
    29	
    30	The rest of this document is the reference for ongoing contributors.
    31	
    32	---
    33	
    34	## Submitting Issues
    35	
    36	All feature requests, bug reports, and general issues should be submitted through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues). Please search for existing issues before opening a new one.
    37	
    38	For security-related issues, see the Security section below.
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## Security
    43	
    44	If you discover a security vulnerability, **do not report it through GitHub Issues**. Instead, please follow the instructions in our [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) file for responsible disclosure. All security reports are kept confidential as described in SECURITY.md.
    45	
    46	---
    47	
    48	## Contributions & Communication
    49	
    50	Contributions and communications are expected to occur through:
    51	
    52	- [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) - Bug reports and feature requests
    53	- [Discord](https://discord.gg/jZJs3Tue4S) - Questions, general conversation, and real-time support
    54	
    55	Please represent the project and community respectfully in all public and private interactions.
    56	
    57	
    58	## How to Contribute
    59	
    60	
    61	There are many ways to contribute:
    62	
    63	- **Feature requests** - Open a [GitHub Issue](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) to discuss your idea
    64	- **Bug reports** - Report issues via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues) (see [Reporting Bugs](#reporting-bugs))
    65	- **Code contributions** - Fix bugs, add features, improve tests
    66	- **Documentation** - Improve guides, fix typos, add examples
    67	- **Community** - Help others, answer questions, share knowledge
    68	
    69	
    70	## Reporting Bugs
    71	
    72	Good bug reports help us fix issues quickly. When reporting a bug, please include:
    73	
    74	### Required Information
    75	
    76	1. **Entire CLI version** - run `entire version`
    77	2. **Operating system**
    78	3. **Go version** - run `go version`
    79	
    80	### What to Include
    81	
    82	Please answer these questions in your bug report:
    83	
    84	1. **What did you do?** - Include the exact commands you ran
    85	2. **What did you expect to happen?**
    86	3. **What actually happened?** - Include the full error message or unexpected output
    87	4. **Can you reproduce it?** - Does it happen every time or intermittently?
    88	5. **Any additional context?** - Logs, screenshots, or related issues
    89	
    90	---
    91	
    92	## Local Setup
    93	
    94	### Prerequisites
    95	
    96	- **Go 1.27.1+** - Check with `go version`. `go.mod` pins the minimum, so an older toolchain fails unless it can download the pinned one (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local` cannot).
    97	- **mise** - Task runner and version manager. Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`
    98	
    99	### Clone and Install
   100	
   101	```bash
   102	# Clone the repository
   103	git clone https://github.com/entireio/cli.git
   104	cd cli

   106	# Trust the mise configuration (required on first setup)

   110	mise install

  1520	func validateTrailUpdateFields(inputs trailUpdateInputs) error {
  1670	// Three dispatch modes, in order:
  1671	//
  1672	//   - overwrite: sends Overwrite: true and no If-Match. This is the explicit
  1673	//     --overwrite flag — the caller wants the replacement to win regardless of
  1674	//     what's there.
  1675	//   - ifMatch non-empty (and !overwrite): sends If-Match instead of Overwrite,
  1676	//     so the write is rejected with 412 if the description changed since
  1677	//     ifMatch was read (resolveTrailUpdateBody / the non-interactive etag
  1678	//     fetch in runTrailUpdateWithClient).
  1679	//   - neither: sends neither If-Match nor Overwrite. This keeps trails without
  1680	//     a body document and servers that omit the etag usable without granting
  1681	//     unconditional replacement authority: the route accepts an empty body
  1682	//     document and rejects a non-empty one with 409.
  1683	func sendTrailBody(ctx context.Context, client *api.Client, path, body, ifMatch string, overwrite bool) error {
  1684		req := api.TrailBodyRequest{Markdown: body}
  1685		var headers http.Header
  1686		if overwrite {
  1687			req.Overwrite = true
  1688		} else if ifMatch != "" {
  1689			headers = http.Header{"If-Match": []string{ifMatch}}
  1690		}
  1691	
  1692		data, err := json.Marshal(req)
  1693		if err != nil {
  1694			return fmt.Errorf("marshal trail body request: %w", err)
  1695		}
  1696		resp, err := client.Request(ctx, http.MethodPut, path, headers, bytes.NewReader(data))
  1697		if err != nil {
  1698			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update trail body: %w", err)
  1699		}
  1700		defer resp.Body.Close()
  1701		if err := checkTrailResponse(resp); err != nil {
  1702			switch {
  1703			case api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusPreconditionFailed):
  1704				return fmt.Errorf("%w — trail body changed since it was read; run 'entire trail show' to see the current text and merge it in, then re-run — or pass --overwrite to discard it", err)
  1705			case api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusConflict):
  1706				return fmt.Errorf("%w — trail body is not empty; pass --overwrite to replace it", err)
  1707			default:
  1708				return err
  1709			}
  1710		}
  1711		// Nothing reads the document back; decoding it only confirms the success
  1712		// really was this route's JSON response, and drains the body — the same
  1713		// check sendTrailPatch makes on the metadata route.
  1714		var doc api.TrailBodyDocument
  1715		if err := api.DecodeJSON(resp, &doc); err != nil {
  1716			return fmt.Errorf("failed to decode trail body response: %w", err)
  1717		}
  1718		return nil
  1719	}

  1671	//

  1673	//     --overwrite flag — the caller wants the replacement to win regardless of
  1674	//     what's there.

  1676	//     so the write is rejected with 412 if the description changed since
  1677	//     ifMatch was read (resolveTrailUpdateBody / the non-interactive etag
  1678	//     fetch in runTrailUpdateWithClient).

  1681	//     unconditional replacement authority: the route accepts an empty body
  1682	//     document and rejects a non-empty one with 409.

  1686		if overwrite {
  1687			req.Overwrite = true
  1688		} else if ifMatch != "" {
  1689			headers = http.Header{"If-Match": []string{ifMatch}}

  1697		if err != nil {
  1698			return fmt.Errorf("failed to update trail body: %w", err)
  1699		}

  1702			switch {
  1703			case api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusPreconditionFailed):
  1704				return fmt.Errorf("%w — trail body changed since it was read; run 'entire trail show' to see the current text and merge it in, then re-run — or pass --overwrite to discard it", err)
  1705			case api.IsHTTPErrorStatus(err, http.StatusConflict):
  1706				return fmt.Errorf("%w — trail body is not empty; pass --overwrite to replace it", err)

## Summary

Make default Trail body updates fail closed when the CLI cannot establish the
current body version.

Only an explicit `--overwrite` now authorizes unconditional replacement.

## Problem

`entire trail update --body` performs a detail GET to obtain the current body
ETag. If that read failed, the command warned and continued with
`overwrite: true`.

A transient read failure therefore became permission to replace content the
caller could not verify. A combined metadata/body update could also apply the
metadata PATCH before discovering that body verification had failed.

The same unsafe fallback existed in the interactive path: a failed seed read
could leave the form editing an incomplete baseline.

## Cause

PR #2079 added ETag and `If-Match` support while retaining a missing-ETag
fallback to `overwrite: true`. Commit d3f920f introduced that compatibility
fallback, and 0dc4af added a warning when the verification read failed without
changing the fallback.

Their checkpoint transcripts are unavailable, so this rationale is based on
the commits and PR description rather than recorded session transcripts.

## Fix

- Return `could not load current trail body` when the interactive seed read
  fails, before opening the form or writing anything.
- Perform the non-interactive body verification before any metadata PATCH.
- Return `could not verify trail body is unchanged` when that read fails.
- Send `overwrite: true` only for explicit `--overwrite`.
- Send `If-Match` when an ETag is available.
- When a successful older/partial response has no ETag, send neither
  `If-Match` nor overwrite authority and rely on the body route's empty-document
  guard.
- Remove the helper error writer that was only used by the deleted warnings.

## Safety invariant

Inability to establish the current Trail body version is not authority to
replace it.

A default body update must fail closed. Only explicit `--overwrite` may perform
an unconditional replacement.

## Compatibility

The current public cell OpenAPI documents `overwrite` as optional and defaulting
to false. Without `overwrite` or a matching `If-Match`, an existing nonempty
body is rejected with 409 rather than replaced.

PR #2055 records the same deployed behavior before detail ETags were usable:
the first write against an empty document succeeded, while a nonempty document
returned `409 document_not_empty`.

This keeps absent and empty bodies writable without granting replacement
authority. Literal omission of `bodyDocument` is treated as older/partial-server
tolerance; current OpenAPI requires both `bodyDocument` and its ETag.
